mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust residential construction, which typically precedes stronger consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy that typically compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signal a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling) occurs but the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained regime (INDPRO growth rate below 1% annually), weak industrial activity typically leads to lower corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO growth rate < 1% annually, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in CPIAUCSL signals rising inflation, which typically leads to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate below 3.5% signals an extremely tight labor market that often triggers wage inflation and central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 3.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which typically drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (HOUST rising and RSAFS rising) occurs but the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary easing regime (FEDFUNDS below 1.0%), the central bank's accommodative policy typically stimulates economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
